root.label: Supreme Court agrees to hear Kentucky shrine zoning dispute

events.label: Supreme Court agrees to hear Kentucky shrine zoning dispute

slots.name: grotto dimensions
slots.sentence: At the center of the case is a proposed 16-by-39-foot grotto that court records say would include a shrine to the Virgin Mary, a plaza, walking path and retaining wall.

slots.name: grotto footprint
slots.sentence: Gardner compared its roughly 600-square-foot footprint to the size of a swimming pool.

slots.name: RLUIPA enactment year
slots.sentence: Gardner said lower courts have developed different approaches to the law since Congress enacted it in 2000, leaving religious organizations with different levels of protection depending on where a dispute arises.

slots.name: zoning ordinance year
slots.sentence: Park Hills’ zoning ordinance adopted in 1974.

slots.name: grotto height
slots.sentence: Neighbors who had raised concerns that the 39-foot grotto would worsen traffic problems sued, arguing that granting the conditional use permit violated state and federal law.

slots.name: review status
slots.sentence: The justices agreed Thursday to take up the request from Missionaries of St. John the Baptist, a church in the Cincinnati suburbs that was denied a permit to construct a large grotto honoring the Virgin Mary in an adjacent lot.
